problem: Existing VLM-based EQA agents treat exploration as one planning problem driven only by local observations, and ignore structural priors such as floorplans that could reveal which unseen room types are question-relevant.
motivation: Answering an EQA question may require discovering a new room, getting a better view of an observed object, or exploring a known room, and these need different strategies. Humans use room-layout priors (e.g., look for a bed in a bedroom); floorplans or building models are often available to robots but unused by EQA methods.
key_idea: A hierarchical VLM planner over an online 3D scene graph and a topological floorplan selects among three exploration modes (explore_room, go_to_objects, find_room), with floorplan-weighted semantic frontier scoring for room discovery.
insight: The floorplan helps only when used structurally: removing FP drops SR from 75.0 to 64.8 (OpenEQA) and 63.2 to 53.5 (ExploreEQA), while simply adding the floorplan to GraphEQA's prompt gives mixed results (43.5 vs 46.3 on OpenEQA, 57.0 vs 54.4 on ExploreEQA). Viewpoint selection and semantic frontiers also each contribute. Gains persist with ground-truth semantics, so they are not just perception fixes.
method: Hierarchical scene graph: Hydra-based online graph with rooms (labels + CLIP key views), objects (YOLOe), navigation nodes (GVD) and open-vocabulary frontiers (LSeg CLIP features fused in a TSDF occupancy map, WFD detection).

Floorplan prior: topological graph of room labels and adjacency (from HM3D annotations in sim, manual in the real world), treated as a weak, possibly noisy prior with no metric geometry or localization.

High-level VLM planner: takes question, choices, JSON scene graph and floorplan, relevant visual memory (top-M=3 CLIP-relevant key views per room + object views + current image) and history; outputs mode, target, answer and confidence, and answers when confidence >= 0.8.
explore_room: restricts to frontiers in the target room and scores them by max CLIP similarity to N=6 VLM-predicted relevant objects.
go_to_objects: samples viewpoints around the target object at a radius set by its bounding box and FoV, scoring them 0.7*mesh-vertex visibility + 0.3*in-image coverage.

find_room: treats all floorplan nodes matching the current room class as candidate locations, computes softmax(-shortest-path distance to target class) weights over neighbour classes, and scores frontiers as 0.35*transition (doorway-to-target prompts) + 0.55*floorplan-weighted + 0.1*frontier size.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o / GPT-5.5 / Gemini-3.5 Pro / Claude Opus 4.8 / Qwen3.5-9B (frozen) as high-level planner; YOLOe, LSeg, CLIP perception
setting.observation: posed RGB-D (plus LiDAR/IMU odometry on the real robot)
setting.action_space: high-level mode selection (explore_room / go_to_objects / find_room) with frontier or viewpoint goals and path planning
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes) plus real quadruped robot
setting.privileged: estimated topological floorplan (built from HM3D semantic annotations in sim, manually in the real world); ground-truth semantics only in the GT analysis

numbers.eval_set_note: 108 single-floor episodes with semantic annotations (HM3D), multiple-choice
108 single-floor episodes with semantic annotations (HM3D), multiple-choice
114 single-floor episodes with semantic annotations (HM3D), multiple-choice

numbers_note: The paper ran no full official splits; both benchmarks are filtered to single-floor episodes with semantic annotations. Results are reported for several VLMs, and only the main ones are listed here. Real-world results are qualitative (Table 4).
results: HFLEX-EQA beats GraphEQA and ExploreEQA in SR across all five VLMs on both datasets. It reaches up to 75.0% on OpenEQA and 63.2% on ExploreEQA, against strongest baselines of 59.3% (ExploreEQA, GPT-5.5) and 54.4% (GraphEQA/ExploreEQA-style, Gemini-3.5) respectively. It uses more steps and longer paths than GraphEQA, and it answered all seven real-robot questions correctly.
limitations: Requires a floorplan prior (from HM3D annotations or manually built) and is evaluated only on single-floor episodes; the floorplan is not automatically estimated.
Depends on proprietary VLM APIs, with more steps and longer paths than GraphEQA, and answer success drops under strong blur.
Real-world evaluation is small (7 qualitative questions) and the no-choice runs were replays of recorded episodes.
